current.text: Washington added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa, and these three will take most of the usage. This cuts into the roles of the young players.
He is likely to get fewer minutes and fewer rim contests with Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr on the roster.
His block rate (26.2% of rim contests turned into blocks) could fall back toward average.
The fifth starter spot is open, with many wings competing for it. A July projection named Kyshawn George as the fifth starter next to Young, Dybantsa, Davis and Sarr.
His defense could make him a candidate to start at shooting guard. In past seasons the team always put him back in the lineup after injuries.
Washington has a deep group of long wings and guards. A 10 or 11 man rotation is expected, with 12 or 13 players who could justify minutes.
Washington is trying to compete and is projected near 40 wins and the play-in, so the late-season resting and minutes cuts of past years should not happen.
Head coach Brian Keefe is under pressure to win this season.
He is not a draft target in our 144-player auction. He is a waiver option to watch early in the season.

durable.text: He is a shot-blocking wing who shows some flashes as a passer.
Steals and blocks are his best categories, and his blocks are strong for a G,F. He is below the pool in FG%, FT%, 3PM, PTS, REB and AST.
He is a poor shooter. His three-point percentage fell from 34% as a rookie to 29% by the end of last season.
Shooting is what holds him back, and he has stalled on offense. One expert partly blames injuries for the shooting drop.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD (rank 208 Yahoo, 180 ESPN), and only 144 players get drafted, so do not draft him. He was not drafted in our league last season either. Without a starting role he is a steals and blocks wing (1.2 STL and 0.9 BLK projected) who hurts FG% at 42.6% and adds little else. Early in the season, check whether he wins the open fifth starter spot and plays more than about 24 minutes. Pick him up on waivers only if he does.
